title: Static Type Checker for Tiny Expression Language
description: A type inference function walks AST nodes (Num, Bool_, Add, If, Not) checking constraints without executing: Add requires Int children, If requires Bool condition and same-type branches, Not requires Bool.

steps.description: Dataclass definitions for the expression language: Num and Bool_ hold values; Add has left/right; If has cond/then_e/else_e; Not has expr. These form the AST node types.
infer_type uses isinstance checks. Num returns Int; Bool_ returns Bool. Add recursively checks both children are Int, raising TypeError with descriptive messages if not.
Lines 22-25: left and right types are inferred recursively; each must equal "Int" or an error is raised showing which side failed.

steps.question: What type does Add(Num(1), Bool_(True)) produce, and what error message?
steps.answer: TypeError: Add: right must be Int, got Bool

steps.description: Not requires Bool child and returns Bool. If checks condition is Bool, then checks then_e and else_e have the same type (tt == te), returning that common type.
Lines 36-38: branch types must match exactly; the type checker cannot know which branch runs at runtime, so both must agree.
run_eval evaluates expressions normally. run calls infer_type first (static check), then run_eval, printing both type and value.
Three well-typed expressions run: Add(Num(1),Num(2)) -> Type: Int Value: 3; If(Bool_(True),Num(1),Num(2)) -> Type: Int Value: 1; Not(Bool_(False)) -> Type: Bool Value: True.
Three type errors caught statically: Add(Int,Bool) fails on right operand; If(Int cond) fails on condition; If branches Int vs Bool fails on mismatched branch types.
